mainTopic: Does an advance הפרה (cancelling a vow before it is made) let the vow take hold for a moment and then cancel it (חיילין ובטלין), or does it stop the vow from ever taking hold (לא חיילין), according to רבי אליעזר?
overview: The גמרא is trying to work out what רבי אליעזר holds when a husband cancels his wife's vows before she makes them. One option is that the vows take hold for a moment and are then cancelled (חיילין ובטלין). The other is that they never take hold at all (לא חיילין). First the גמרא brings the end of a ברייתא, where the רבנן answer רבי אליעזר with an argument about immersing a vessel in advance. That seems to show the vows take hold for a moment. The גמרא pushes this proof aside: the רבנן were not sure of his reasoning, so they gave a counter-argument for each possibility. Next it brings רבי אליעזר's own קל וחומר from seeds already planted in the ground. That seems to show the vows never take hold at all. Finally the גמרא asks why the רבנן reject his קל וחומר, when another ברייתא shows them using a very similar one about selling a daughter who is a נערה. The answer to that question comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא suggests the vows take hold and are then cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the רבנן's answer to רבי אליעזר about immersing a vessel in advance. It concludes that, as they understood him, an advance הפרה lets the vow take hold for a moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the ברייתא. The רבנן said to רבי אליעזר: we immerse an impure vessel to make it pure. So should someone immerse a vessel now, so that later, when it becomes impure, it will already be purified? This shows the vows take hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the end of the ברייתא to show that the vows do take hold for a moment. The רבנן's challenge about the vessel only makes sense if that is how they understood רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel immersed ahead of time still becomes impure later; the earlier immersion does not help. The רבנן compare this to an advance הפרה, so they seem to think רבי אליעזר holds that the vow takes hold and is then cancelled. If so, their point is that this mechanism cannot work for a vessel either.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (look at) the last part of the source
Immersing something in a מקוה to make it pure
For when it later becomes impure
They take effect (the vows take hold)

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
phrases.notes: He means the end of the same ברייתא that was just quoted.

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Eliezer:
If one immerses an impure vessel to purify it,
shall one immerse a vessel so that when it becomes impure it will be purified?
Learn from this: they take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the end of the ברייתא from the previous discussion to argue for חיילין ובטלין.
steps.raayaObject: According to רבי אליעזר, vows cancelled in advance take hold for a moment and are then cancelled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רבנן's answer in the ברייתא comparing it to immersing a vessel before it becomes impure.

steps.title: The רבנן were not sure of his reasoning and answered both ways
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed aside. The רבנן did not know which way רבי אליעזר holds, so they gave a counter-argument for each possibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: the רבנן could not figure out רבי אליעזר's reason. So they said to him: what do you hold? If you hold the vows take hold and are then cancelled, the vessel case refutes you. If you hold they never take hold, the מקוה case refutes you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the previous step. The vessel argument does not show what רבי אליעזר really holds; it is only one half of a two-sided answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן built a 'whichever way you hold' argument. The vessel example only targets the possibility that the vows take hold and are then cancelled. A different example, the מקוה, targets the possibility that they never take hold. So their words tell us nothing about what רבי אליעזר actually holds.

keyTerms.meaning: They could not pin down his reasoning
They take hold and are then cancelled

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the רבנן's argument tells us what רבי אליעזר really holds. The רבנן were attacking both possible readings of his view.

phrases.english: They say:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנַן לָא קָיְימִי לְהוֹן בְּטַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: The Rabbis could not determine the reasoning of Rabbi Eliezer,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכִי קָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ: מַאי סְבִירָא לָךְ?
phrases.english: and this is what they said to him: What do you hold?
If you hold that they take effect and are then nullified,
the vessel will be your refutation;
if you do not hold that they take effect,
the ritual bath will be your refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: רַבָּנַן לָא קָיְימִי לְהוֹן בְּטַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that רבי אליעזר holds חיילין ובטלין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The vessel argument was only one branch of a two-sided challenge, not a statement of his actual view.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's argument from seeds suggests the vows never take hold
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues from seeds: impure seeds become pure once planted, so seeds already planted surely stay pure. This suggests that an advance הפרה stops the vow from ever taking hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אליעזר said to them: impure seeds become pure once they are planted in the ground. So seeds that are already planted, all the more so they stay pure! This shows the vows do not take hold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof, this time from רבי אליעזר's own words. It points the other way: the vows never take hold at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planted seeds that touch impurity don't become impure for even a moment; they are simply protected. רבי אליעזר compares the advance הפרה to this. So it seems the vow is blocked from the start rather than taking hold and then being cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: Already planted and standing in the ground
Is it not all the more so?

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Eliezer said to them:
And just as impure seeds,
once one has sown them in the ground, are pure,
those already sown,
phrases.notes: Seeds that were already in the ground when they touched something impure.

phrases.english: is it not all the more so?
Learn from this: they do not take effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous proof was rejected, a new proof is brought for the opposite view.
steps.raayaObject: According to רבי אליעזר, vows cancelled in advance never take hold (לא חיילין).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר from impure seeds that become pure once planted.

steps.title: Don't the רבנן use this kind of קל וחומר elsewhere?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן reject רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר. A ברייתא shows them using the same kind of reasoning about selling a daughter who is a נערה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן don't learn from a קל וחומר? But a ברייתא teaches: could a man sell his daughter as a maidservant when she is a נערה? You can say a קל וחומר: a girl already sold goes free when she becomes a נערה. So a girl who was never sold, isn't it logical that she cannot be sold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the רבנן. Why do they reject רבי אליעזר's reasoning when they accept the same kind of reasoning in another ברייתא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter argument has the same shape as רבי אליעזר's. If becoming a נערה ends a sale that already happened, it surely stops a new sale from starting. In the same way, if a husband can cancel a vow that already took hold, he should surely be able to stop one in advance. Since the רבנן use the first argument, why not the second?

keyTerms.meaning: An 'all the more so' argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
A girl who has reached the first stage of maturity

steps.whyThisMatters: It forces the גמרא to explain what makes רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר different from one the רבנן themselves accept.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, do they not derive from an a fortiori inference?
But isn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם אֶת בִּתּוֹ כְּשֶׁהִיא נַעֲרָה?
phrases.english: Could a person sell his daughter as a maidservant when she is a young woman?
You can say an a fortiori inference:
one already sold goes free,
phrases.notes: She goes free when she becomes a נערה.

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ מְכוּרָה — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא תִּימָּכֵר?
phrases.english: one not yet sold, is it not logical that she cannot be sold?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן לָא דָּרְשִׁי קַל וָחוֹמֶר? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what רבי אליעזר holds to why the רבנן reject his קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's rejection of רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן accept a קל וחומר with the same structure in the case of selling a נערה. Rejecting it here looks inconsistent.
